1.sa: श्रीमल्लक्ष्मीनृसिंहस्य श्रियं दिशतु मे नखः । स्वभक्ताभीष्टदानाय समुपात्तदशाकृतेः ॥ १0 ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Let the claws of Lord Sri Narasimha who has taken ten different incarnations for the purpose of bestowing the deserving men and women who are devoted to Him with the four objects of a soul viz Dharma - Artha - Kama - Moksha bless me with prosperity.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: श्रीमल्लक्ष्मीनृसिंहस्य श्रियम् दिशतु मे नखः स्वभक्ताभीष्टदानाय समुपात्तदशाकृतेः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: स्वभक्ताभीष्टदानाय समुपात्तदशाकृतेः श्रीमल्लक्ष्मीनृसिंहस्य नखः मे श्रियम् दिशतु।
commentaries.gemini_summary: May the claw of the glorious Lord Lakshmi-Narasimha, who assumes ten divine incarnations to bestow all desired blessings upon His devotees, grant me spiritual and material prosperity.

2.sa: वस्तु स्तुतं सुरस्तोमैरस्तु शस्तं मया स्तुतम् । मस्तुहस्तं प्रस्तुताय श्रुतिमस्तकविश्रुतम् ॥ २ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: I extol and pray Lord Sri Krishna who is crawling holding butter in one hand and who is expounded by the Vedas and Brahmameemamsa and whom Sri Lakshmi and all the devatas eulogise constantly, to bestow his blessings on me in the onerous task of successful completion of this literary work.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: वस्तु स्तुतम् सुर-स्तोमैः अस्तु शस्तम् मया स्तुतम् मस्तु-हस्तम् प्रस्तुताय श्रुति-मस्तक-विश्रुतम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: सुर-स्तोमैः स्तुतं मस्तु-हस्तं श्रुति-मस्तक-विश्रुतं वस्तु मया स्तुतं प्रस्तुताय शस्तम् अस्तु ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: May the Supreme Being (Lord Krishna), who holds butter in His hand, is renowned in the Upanishads, and is worshipped by multitudes of gods, bestow auspiciousness upon the work undertaken as He is praised by me.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The sea swells at the sight of full moon rising. Likewise I wish that refined and meaningful rhetoric words which inspire me to complete the noble task of writing this literary work flash on my mind at the reminiscence of Sri Madhwacharya who is the embodiment of great erudition and a treasure of complete knowledge.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: श्रीमदानन्दतीर्थ-इन्दु-भासनम् मम मानसे आशासे साधु-शब्द-अर्थ-सरिदीश-अभिवृद्धये
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: साधुशब्दार्थसरिदीशाभिवृद्धये मम मानसे श्रीमदानन्दतीर्थेन्दुभासनम् आशासे ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The author prays for the moon-like brilliance of Sri Anandatirtha (Madhwacharya) to shine in his mind, so that the ocean of worthy words and rich meanings may swell and flourish for this literary work.

4.sa: श्रीराघवेन्द्ररत्नानां रसनारङ्गनर्तकी । शब्दाम्बुधिशरज्ज्योत्स्ना शरणं मम शारदा ॥ ४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The tongue of Sri Raghavendra on whose face the resplendence of a gem is constantly manifested serves as the stage for Sri Vidyadevi to performs dance, where she merrily dances and transform into meaningful and resourceful words resulting from the discourses and commentaries by the great saint. Let that Sri Vidyadevi infuse me with waves of meaningful words as the moon light of an autumn swells the ocean.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: श्रीराघवेन्द्ररत्नानाम् रसनारङ्गनर्तकी शब्दाम्बुधिशरज्ज्योत्स्ना शरणम् मम शारदा
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: श्रीराघवेन्द्ररत्नानाम् रसनारङ्गनर्तकी शब्दाम्बुधिशरज्ज्योत्स्ना शारदा मम शरणम्
commentaries.gemini_summary: May Goddess Sharada (Sarasvati), who dances gracefully on the stage of Sri Raghavendra's tongue and who illuminates and swells the ocean of eloquence like autumnal moonlight, be my refuge.

5.sa: कठिनापि कविश्लाघ्या त्रिविक्रमसरस्वती । सुवर्णयोगसन्दृश्या वरा वज्रमणिर्यथा ॥ ५ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Diamond though very hard gets appreciation from the experts when they scrutinise the gold ornaments studded with diamonds. Only then one can appraise it. Likewise, though the points of view of Trivikramapanditacharya in his literary masterpieces like Ushaharna, Harivayustuti, Vishnustuti, Tattvadeepa and others cannot be easily apprehended, those views receive adoration from the scholarly poets as they are composed with rhetoric and rhyming words. Let those words inspire me in my task of writing this book.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: कठिना अपि कविश्लाघ्या त्रिविक्रमसरस्वती सुवर्णयोगसन्दृश्या वरा वज्रमणिः यथा
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यथा सुवर्णयोगसन्दृश्या कठिना अपि वरा वज्रमणिः (श्लाघ्या भवति), तथा सुवर्णयोगसन्दृश्या कठिना अपि त्रिविक्रमसरस्वती कविश्लाघ्या (अस्ति)।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Just as a superior diamond, though extremely hard, is admired by experts when set in fine gold, so too the composition of Trivikrama Pandita, though challenging and dense, is praised by wise poets when appreciated for its brilliant phrasing and meter.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The words of Narayanapanditacharya which are dexterously glowing in his literary gems in different genrs like Sri Sumadhwavijaya, Sangraha Ramayana, Shubodaya, Parijataharana and others resemble the mellifluous sound of the veena adorning the hands of Sri Vidyadevi.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: वाणी पाणितल-आसक्त-वीणा-रव-विडम्बिनी नाना-प्रबन्ध-चतुरा भाति नारायण-आर्य-गीः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: पाणितलासक्तवीणारवविडम्बिनी नानाप्रबन्धचतुरा नारायणार्यगीः वाणी भाति ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The eloquent poetic speech of Sri Narayanapanditacharya, adept across diverse literary compositions, shines like Goddess Sarasvati herself, rivalling the melodious music of the veena resting in her hands.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The words of Sri Vyasaraja which are splendidly shining like a coral tree in the garden of the doctrine of Sri Madhwacharya taste very sweet like the sap of flowers in the coral tree of the devathas. Let those words bring me success prays the author.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: वृन्दार-वन-मन्दार-मकरन्द-सहोदरी विश्रुता विजयम् दद्यात् व्यासतीर्थ-आर्य-भारती
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: वृन्दार-वन-मन्दार-मकरन्द-सहोदरी विश्रुता व्यासतीर्थ-आर्य-भारती विजयम् दद्यात्।
commentaries.gemini_summary: May the renowned speech of the venerable Sri Vyasatirtha, which is as sweet as the nectar of the Mandara flowers in the celestial garden of the gods, bestow victory.

8.sa: व्याससूत्रपदार्थोपन्यासमाकर्ण्य मान्यपि । व्यासराजस्य भजते दासतां को न कोविदः ॥ ८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Any scholar though full of pride and egoism is sure to go into a state of ecstasy when he listens to and ruminates the views expressed by Sri Vyasaraja in 'Chandrika', his magnum opus while explicating the incomprehensible meanings of Sri Vedavyasa's Brahmasutras. All such scholars are sure to eschew their pride and become the disciples of the great saint.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: व्याससूत्रपदार्थोपन्यासम् आकर्ण्य मानी अपि व्यासराजस्य भजते दासताम् कः न कोविदः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: व्यासराजस्य व्याससूत्रपदार्थोपन्यासम् आकर्ण्य मानी अपि कः कोविदः दासताम् न भजते
commentaries.gemini_summary: Upon hearing Vyasaraja's profound exposition of the meanings of Vyasa's Brahmasutras, what scholar—however proud—would not become his devoted disciple?

9.sa: चतुःषष्टिकलाविद्याजुषे विद्वन्महोजुषे । जयीन्द्रज्योतिषे कुर्या वन्दनानि यशोमुषे ॥ ९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: I reverentially pay my obeisance to the scholarly radiance of Sri Vijayeendra Theertha who is well versed in all the Sixty four arts and who has his fame spread all over for his sagacity in destroying the lustre of the rival scholars in disputations.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: चतुःषष्टि-कला-विद्या-जुषे विद्वत्-महः-जुषे जयीन्द्र-ज्योतिषे कुर्याम् वन्दनानि यशः-मुषे
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: चतुःषष्टि-कला-विद्या-जुषे विद्वत्-महः-जुषे यशः-मुषे जयीन्द्र-ज्योतिषे वन्दनानि कुर्याम्।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The poet offers his reverent salutations to the radiant spiritual master Sri Vijayindra Tirtha, who is adept in the sixty-four traditional arts, abounds in the brilliance of erudition, and eclipses the fame of rival scholars in disputation.

10.sa: सुधीन्द्रयोगिनं सेवे साधुसत्कृतसंपदम् । स गद्यपद्यनिर्माणविद्यायाः प्रथमं पदम् ॥ १० ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: I adore with profound devotion Sri Sudheendra Theertha who has his affluence distributed amongst the virtuous and who is in the forefront of the group of scholars by virtue of his extraordinary competence in writing scholarly literary works whether in the form of prose or poetry.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: सुधीन्द्रयोगिनम् सेवे साधुसत्कृतसंपदम् सः गद्यपद्यनिर्माणविद्यायाः प्रथमम् पदम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: साधुसत्कृतसंपदम् सुधीन्द्रयोगिनम् सेवे । सः गद्यपद्यनिर्माणविद्यायाः प्रथमम् पदम् (अस्ति) ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The poet offers his adoration to the ascetic Sudheendra Teertha, whose wealth is dedicated to and honored by the virtuous, and who stands foremost in the mastery of composing prose and poetry.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: All the wishes like marriage, children, pristine devotion, profound knowledge, oratory skill, robust health, etc of those will get fulfilled if they surrender before the lotus feet for Sri Raghavendra theertha who is the embodiment of virtues such as Jnana (Knowledge) - Bhakti (Devotion) - Vairagya (Renunciation). I reverentially bow my head at those sacred feet which are like Kalapavruksha in fulfilling one's wishes.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: श्रीमतः राघवेन्द्रस्य नमामि पदपङ्कजे कामित-अशेष-कल्याण-कलना-कल्पपादपौ
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अहम् कामिताशेषकल्याणकलनाकल्पपादपौ श्रीमतः राघवेन्द्रस्य पदपङ्कजे नमामि ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: I bow to the lotus feet of the venerable Sri Raghavendra, which act like the wish-fulfilling Kalpavriksha tree in bestowing all desired auspicious blessings.

12.sa: मुहुः स्मारितवाल्मीकिं पुनस्तं नौमि दैशिकम् । यो विस्तीर्णां रामकथां स्रग्धराभिः समग्रहीत् ॥ १२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: I once again extol Sri Raghavendra who in his Ramacharitramanjari has compendiously abridged the entire story of Valmiki Ramayana as narrated by Sri Madhwacharaya in Mahabharata Tatparya Nirnaya to just eleven stanzas composed in Sragdhara Scale. The picture of Valmiki comes into one's mind whenever he reads Ramacharitramanjari just as it does when the epic of Ramayana is read.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: मुहुः स्मारित-वाल्मीकिम् पुनः तम् नौमि दैशिकम् यः विस्तीर्णाम् राम-कथाम् स्रग्धराभिः समग्रहीत्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यः विस्तीर्णां रामकथां स्रग्धराभिः समग्रहीत् मुहुः स्मारितवाल्मीकिं तं दैशिकं पुनः नौमि ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: I bow once again to that revered preceptor (Sri Raghavendra) who brings Sage Valmiki repeatedly to mind, having condensed the vast epic of Rama into verses of the Sragdhara metre.

13.sa: मूकोऽपि यत्प्रसादेन मुकुन्दशयनायते । राजराजायते रिक्तो राघवेन्द्रं तमाश्रये ॥ १३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Even a born dumb and deaf transforms into a fine orator like Shesha, the couch of Lord Sri Narayana, even and impecunious becomes an affluent with the blessings of Sri Raghavendra. I offer my obeisance to the lotus feet of that great Saint and pray for his blessings in composing this poetry.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: मूकः अपि यत्प्रसादेन मुकुन्दशयनायते राजराजायते रिक्तः राघवेन्द्रम् तम् आश्रये
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यत्प्रसादेन मूकः अपि मुकुन्दशयनायते रिक्तः राजराजायते तं राघवेन्द्रम् आश्रये
commentaries.gemini_summary: I take refuge in Sri Raghavendra, by whose grace even a mute becomes eloquent like Adishesha (the bed of Lord Mukunda) and a pauper becomes wealthy like Kubera.

14.sa: प्रसाद्य नरपञ्चास्यं प्राप्तं वैदुष्यमद्भुतम् । येन लक्ष्मीनृसिंहेन तातपादं तमाश्रये ॥ १४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: I offer my respects to my father Sri Lakshminarasimhacharya who has attained great scholarship by his act of pleasing Lord Sri Lakshmi Narasimha with his worship and meditation.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: प्रसाद्य नरपञ्चास्यम् प्राप्तम् वैदुष्यम् अद्भुतम् येन लक्ष्मीनृसिंहेन तातपादम् तम् आश्रये
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: येन लक्ष्मीनृसिंहेन नरपञ्चास्यम् प्रसाद्य अद्भुतम् वैदुष्यम् प्राप्तम् तम् तातपादम् आश्रये
commentaries.gemini_summary: The poet offers his salutations to his revered father, Lakshminarasimha, who acquired extraordinary scholarship by pleasing the man-lion deity, Lord Narasimha.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: I may be guilty of committing sin of heaping praises on ordinary people driven by my greed. Now I will sanctify my defiled tongue by taking a dip in the Ganges of adulation of Lord Sri Moolaramachandra indwelling in the lotus heart of Sri Raghavendra.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: प्राप्तान्यनुतिपापौघरसनाम् पावयामि अहम् गुर्वन्तर्यामिभगवत्स्तुतिगङ्गाम्बुमज्जनात्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: अहम् गुर्वन्तर्यामिभगवत्स्तुतिगङ्गाम्बुमज्जनात् प्राप्तान्यनुतिपापौघरसनाम् पावयामि ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The poet resolves to purify his tongue, tainted by the sin of having praised other mortal men, by bathing it in the sacred Ganga-like waters of praising the Supreme Lord dwelling within his Guru.

16.sa: कलये कवनं किञ्चित्कवीनां सहवासतः । पाटीरगिरिसान्निध्यान्निम्बद्रुरिव सौरभम् ॥ १६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: A mango tree yields sweet and fragrant fruits. A sandalwood tree which grows abundantly in the vicinity of Malayaparvata spreads a pleasant aroma all over. A neem tree grown near a mango tree or a sandalwood tree though bitter and odourless also generates a sweet fragrance by virtue of its proximity with those trees. Likewise though I am not competent enough to write poetry, I will take up the task of composing this poetry albeit average by all standards by virtue of my association with some learned poets. (Though the author is a great poet, he has made this statement just for condemnation of self egoism).
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: कलये कवनम् किञ्चित् कवीनाम् सहवासतः पाटीरगिरिसान्निध्यात् निम्बद्रुः इव सौरभम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: पाटीरगिरिसान्निध्यात् निम्बद्रुः सौरभम् इव कवीनाम् सहवासतः किञ्चित् कवनम् कलये
commentaries.gemini_summary: The poet humbly expresses that just as a bitter neem tree acquires fragrance due to its proximity to the sandalwood mountain, he is able to compose some poetry through his association with great poets.

17.sa: दृष्टं गुरुप्रसदनमदृष्टं च फलं कृतेः । यथा स्विष्टकृतो ब्रह्मसूत्राद्यप्रणवस्य च ॥ १७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The result of homa is perceptible whereas that of at the beginning of Brahmasutras is imperceptible. But this poetry of mine has the privilege of having both perceptible and imperceptible effects in the form of the blessings of Sri Raghavendra and also in the form of salvation through the grace of Lord Sri Hari.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: दृष्टम् गुरु-प्रसदनम् अदृष्टम् च फलम् कृतेः यथा स्विष्टकृतः ब्रह्म-सूत्र-आद्य-प्रणवस्य च
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यथा स्विष्टकृतः ब्रह्म-सूत्र-आद्य-प्रणवस्य च (फलं भवति), (तथा) कृतेः दृष्टं फलं गुरु-प्रसदनम् अदृष्टं च फलम् (भवति)
commentaries.gemini_summary: Just as the Sviṣṭakṛt ritual offering and the initial Praṇava of the Brahma Sūtras bring seen and unseen results respectively, this literary composition brings both the visible reward of pleasing the Guru and the unseen reward of spiritual merit.

18.sa: श्रेयांसि श्रयते को वा प्रसादेन विना गुरोः । कैवल्यमिव गोविन्दकारुण्येन विना जनः ॥ १८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Is it possible for one to achieve salvation without getting the kind blessings of Lord Sri Govinda who is expounded by the Vedas and Puranas? Likewise, one cannot achieve the four objects of the soul without getting the blessings of guru.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: श्रेयांसि श्रयते कः वा प्रसादेन विना गुरोः कैवल्यम् इव गोविन्दकारुण्येन विना जनः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: गोविन्दकारुण्येन विना कैवल्यम् इव गुरोः प्रसादेन विना कः वा जनः श्रेयांसि श्रयते
commentaries.gemini_summary: Just as a person cannot attain ultimate liberation without the compassion of Lord Govinda, no one can attain spiritual welfare and auspicious attainments without the grace of the Guru.

19.sa: कविताफलमन्यत्किं गुरूणां गुणवर्णनात् । अपवर्गं विनान्यत्किं ब्रह्मजिज्ञासने फलम् ॥ १९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Exploration of thoughts about Brahman results in His blessings and enables one to achieve intuitive knowledge which finally leads him to the path of salvation. A competent poet therefore should employ his talent in extolling the virtues of guru. Then only his effort becomes fruitful.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: कविता-फलम् अन्यत् किम् गुरूणाम् गुण-वर्णनात् अपवर्गम् विना अन्यत् किम् ब्रह्म-जिज्ञासने फलम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: गुरूणाम् गुण-वर्णनात् अन्यत् कविता-फलम् किम् अपवर्गम् विना ब्रह्म-जिज्ञासने अन्यत् फलम् किम्
commentaries.gemini_summary: What other ultimate fruit can poetry have other than describing the noble virtues of the Guru, just as what other fruit can there be in the philosophical inquiry into Brahman besides liberation?

20.sa: गुरुपादरजस्सङ्गाद्विमलं कवनं मम । कलुषं वारि कतकरजसा किं न निर्मलम् ॥ २० ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Does not the muddy water turns crystal clear when treated with clearing nut powder? Similarly, though my composition might not be blemishless because of human errors, it gets sanctified by virtue of its contact with the sacred dust of the lotus feet of guru Sri Raghavendra.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: गुरुपादरजःसङ्गात् विमलं कवनम् मम कलुषम् वारि कतकरजसा किम् न निर्मलम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: मम कवनं गुरुपादरजःसङ्गात् विमलं (भवति), कलुषं वारि कतकरजसा निर्मलं न (भवति) किम् ?
commentaries.gemini_summary: The poet asserts that just as muddy water is made pure and clear by the powder of the clearing-nut (kataka), his poetry becomes completely blemishless and sanctified by its association with the sacred dust of his Guru's feet.

21.sa: रमणीयापि कविता न हृद्या यद्यसत्परा । निसर्गमधुरा दुष्टजिह्वासक्तेव शर्करा ॥ २१ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The tongue of a person suffering from ailments such as bile feels the taste of sweet sugar as bitter. Likewise a poetry composed in glorification of a vicious leader cannot be fascinating even though it is grammatically rich and comprises rhetorical expressions and romantic sentiments.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: रमणीया अपि कविता न हृद्या यदि असत्परा निसर्गमधुरा दुष्टजिह्वासक्ता इव शर्करा
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: कविता रमणीया अपि यदि असत्परा (स्यात्, तर्हि) दुष्टजिह्वासक्ता निसर्गमधुरा शर्करा इव हृद्या न (भवति)।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Even if poetry is naturally charming, it fails to please the heart if it is dedicated to an unworthy or wicked person, just as inherently sweet sugar is not relishable to a diseased tongue.

22.sa: अभव्यमपि मे काव्यं सेव्यं गुरुगुणाश्रयम् । घनाघनगतं वारि यथा लवणवारिधेः ॥ २२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Though sea water is saline, it loses it salinity and tastes sweet when it gets transformed into clouds and pours down as rain. Similarly though my poetry may lack rhetoric sentiments and proficiency, it certainly deserves wide acceptance as it is composed in laudation of the great guru.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: अभव्यम् अपि मे काव्यम् सेव्यम् गुरु-गुण-आश्रयम् घनाघन-गतम् वारि यथा लवण-वारिधेः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यथा लवणवारिधेः घनाघनगतं वारि (सेव्यं भवति), तथा गुरुगुणाश्रयं मे काव्यम् अभव्यम् अपि सेव्यम् (अस्ति)।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Just as the salty water of the ocean becomes pure and drinkable upon entering rain clouds, my poetry, though inherently lacking elegance, becomes worthy of appreciation because it describes the virtues of the Guru.

23.sa: अदोषाप्यगुणेत्युक्तिस्त्यक्तुं युक्ता न मे बुधैः । पतिव्रतागुणेत्येव पत्या किं त्यजते प्रिया ॥ २३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: A husband would never discard his loving wife who possesses a charater of chastity even if she lacks smartness and pulchritude. Likewise it is unfair on the part of the virtuous scholars to ignore this composition of mine even though its portrayal lacks in rhetoric expressions, because it is blemishless as it eulogises the virtues of the great guru.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: अदोषा अपि अगुणा इति उक्तिः त्यक्तुम् युक्ता न मे बुधैः पतिव्रता अगुणा इति एव पत्या किम् त्यजते प्रिया
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: मे उक्तिः अदोषा अपि अगुणा इति बुधैः त्यक्तुम् न युक्ता, पतिव्रता अगुणा इति एव पत्या प्रिया किम् त्यजते
commentaries.gemini_summary: The poet argues that scholars should not discard his flawless composition merely because it lacks poetic ornaments, just as a husband would not abandon a devoted, chaste wife simply because she lacks other charms.

24.sa: अदोषं गुणवद्धृश्यं सर्वैः सर्वार्थदायकम् । परं ब्रह्मेव यत्काव्यं श्रुत्युक्तं तत्तु दुर्लभम् ॥ २४ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: It is very difficult for one to apprehend Parabrahman who is free from all defects; who is attributed with infinite qualities and characteristics like etc; who is understood perceptibly by the enlightened; who bestows the deserving with all the four objects of a soul; whom the Vedas expound. Similarly one finds it hard to come across a composition which is blemishless, which comprises all the distinctive features of a good poetry, which deserves to be read by all the non envious men of scholarship and which is acclaimed even by the Vedas. But this poetry of mine deserves wide acceptance as it has become blemishless with the blessings of Lord Sri Hari-Vayu-Guru.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: अदोषम् गुणवत् दृश्यम् सर्वैः सर्वार्थदायकम् परम् ब्रह्म इव यत् काव्यम् श्रुत्युक्तम् तत् तु दुर्लभम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यत् काव्यम् अदोषम् गुणवत् सर्वैः दृश्यम् सर्वार्थदायकम् श्रुत्युक्तम् परम् ब्रह्म इव (अस्ति), तत् तु दुर्लभम् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: A poetic composition that is entirely flawless, endowed with poetic virtues, worthy of appreciation by all, bestowing all human goals, and conforming to Vedic truth is extremely rare to find, just like the Supreme Brahman.

25.sa: काव्ये गवेषते कश्चिद्दोषमेव गुणं परः । पिचुमन्दं यथा काकः पिकश्चूतलतां यथा ॥ २५ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: A wicked crow goes in search of bitter neem shoot and fruit whereas a cuckoo relishes the sweetness of mango shoot true to their natures. Similarly a censorious looks for defects in a poetry whereas one who is endowed with an aesthetic sense enjoys its characteristic features. It is the inherent quality of the censorious to always look for faults whereas the virtuous always recognise good qualities. Therefore my composition will lose not even a shred of its sheen if one who is wicked tries to find fault in it.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: काव्ये गवेषते कश्चित् दोषम् एव गुणम् परः पिचुमन्दम् यथा काकः पिकः चूतलताम् यथा
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यथा काकः पिचुमन्दम् गवेषते यथा पिकः चूतलताम् गवेषते तथा कश्चित् काव्ये दोषम् एव गवेषते परः गुणम् गवेषते
commentaries.gemini_summary: Just as a crow searches for the bitter neem tree while a cuckoo seeks the sweet mango vine, one person looks only for faults in poetry while another searches for its virtues.

26.sa: अस्मद्गुरूणामाधिक्यं कविः को वाऽनुवर्णयेत् । तथापि तत्प्रसादेन भक्त्या किंचिद्वदाम्यहम् ॥ २६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: My Guru Sri Raghavendra is a treasure of virtues like knowledge, devotion, renunciation, absorption in prayer and meditation. Nobody is competent enough to elaborate on these virtues. Nevertheless, I will try to give a brief description of his distinguished qualities with his blessings and also by drawing strength and inspiration from my profound devotion in him.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: अस्मद्गुरूणाम् आधिक्यम् कविः कः वा अनुवर्णयेत् तथा अपि तत्प्रसादेन भक्त्या किञ्चित् वदामि अहम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: कः वा कविः अस्मद्गुरूणाम् आधिक्यम् अनुवर्णयेत् तथा अपि तत्प्रसादेन भक्त्या अहम् किञ्चित् वदामि
commentaries.gemini_summary: Which poet could ever fully describe the supreme greatness of our Guru? Nevertheless, by his grace and out of deep devotion, I shall speak a little about him.

27.sa: देवानामिब देवेन्द्रो यो दत्त इव योगिनाम् । दुग्धाब्धिरिव सिन्धूनां गुरूणामिव पूर्णधीः ॥ २७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Guru Sri Raghavendra is coruscating like Devendra amidst devatas, shining brilliantly like Dattatreya in the midst of the ascetics, sparking like the sea of milk amongst the oceans. His scholarship of high erudition compares well with that of Sri Anandatheertha, the omniscient whose knowledge stands out as the most superior amongst the knowledge of all Paramahamsas. My mind always concentrates on deliberating the divine prowess of such a great saint.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: देवानाम् इव देवेन्द्रः यः दत्तः इव योगिनाम् दुग्धाब्धिः इव सिन्धूनाम् गुरूणाम् इव पूर्णधीः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यः देवानाम् देवेन्द्रः इव योगिनाम् दत्तः इव सिन्धूनाम् दुग्धाब्धिः इव गुरूणाम् पूर्णधीः इव (अस्ति / भाति)
commentaries.gemini_summary: He shines supreme like Devendra among the gods, Lord Dattatreya among the yogis, the ocean of milk among all seas, and Sri Purnaprajna (Madhvacharya) among all preceptors.

28.sa: तिग्मांशुरिव तेजस्वी शीतांशुरिव शीतलः । यः सिन्धुरिव गम्भीरो धराधर इव स्थिरः ॥ २८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Guru Sri Raghavendra has the resplendence of the sun manifested on his face; he is calm and composed like the coolness of the moon; his majesty resembles that of the ocean; his steadfastness compares well with that of the mountain. I am yearning to extol the saint of such greatness.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: तिग्मांशुः इव तेजस्वी शीतांशुः इव शीतलः यः सिन्धुः इव गम्भीरः धराधरः इव स्थिरः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यः तिग्मांशुः इव तेजस्वी शीतांशुः इव शीतलः सिन्धुः इव गम्भीरः धराधरः इव स्थिरः
commentaries.gemini_summary: This verse describes the greatness of the Guru, who is radiant like the sun, gentle and cooling like the moon, profound and deep like the ocean, and unshakably steadfast like a mountain.

29.sa: शारदाया दयामेव शास्त्राणां परिशीलने । विविधग्रन्थकरणे यः सहायं समाश्रितः ॥ २९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra is well versed in all the shastras like Tarka, Vyakarana, Meemamsa, Vedanta and others. He has written scholarly books in the form of glosses commentaries and condemnations with the lone blessings of Sri Vidya Lakshmi without taking recourse to guidance from others. My mind is always concentrated on the thoughts about the Guru of such greatness.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: शारदायाः दयाम् एव शास्त्राणाम् परिशीलने विविध-ग्रन्थ-करणे यः सहायम् समाश्रितः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यः शास्त्राणां परिशीलने विविध-ग्रन्थ-करणे शारदायाः दयाम् एव सहायं समाश्रितः
commentaries.gemini_summary: He (Sri Raghavendra) relied solely on the grace of Goddess Sharada (Sarasvati) as his aid while thoroughly studying the sacred scriptures and composing a diverse array of scholarly works.

30.sa: वेदव्रजावनोद्युक्तं विद्यादेवी विलोक्य यम् । व्यस्मरद्गहुरूपेण तपस्यन्तं समीरणम् ॥ ३० ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Bharathidevi who observed Sri Raghavendra engaged in protecting the Vedas by writing scholarly literary works and imparting knowledge of Shastras to his disciples appeared like forgetting her consort Sri Vayudeva who was absorbed in penance in three crore different forms. Pleased by the action of protection of the Vedas by Sri Raghavendra in whom rests the special avesha of Sri Vayudeva, Sri Bharathidevi determined to continuously bestow her blessings on him by staying constantly with him. This is the intended meaning of this stanza.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: वेदव्रजावन-उद्युक्तम् विद्यादेवी विलोक्य यम् व्यस्मरत् बहुरूपेण तपस्यन्तम् समीरणम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: विद्यादेवी वेदव्रजावन-उद्युक्तम् यम् विलोक्य बहुरूपेण तपस्यन्तम् समीरणम् व्यस्मरत् ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Seeing Raghavendra actively devoted to protecting the multitude of Vedas, Vidyadevi (Bharati) was so captivated that she forgot even her consort Vayu, who was engaged in severe penance in multiple forms.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The roots of knowledge of the Vedas and other Shastras had remained severed as a result of the influence of Kaliyuga. But the scholarly literary works and the sprinkle of ambrosia in the form of the words of Sri Raghavendra enabled those roots of knowledge to sprout again as the real sprinkle of ambrosia does for the severed roots of a plant. Thus Sri Raghavendra who brought back the roots of Knowledge to life bestowed his blessings on the virtuous by imparting knowledge to them.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: कलिकाल-कला-लून-मूल-जाल-कला लता यत्-वाक्-अमृत-सेकेन पुनः सञ्जात-पल्लवा
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: कलिकाल-कला-लून-मूल-जाल-कला लता यत्-वाक्-अमृत-सेकेन पुनः सञ्जात-पल्लवा (अभवत्)
commentaries.gemini_summary: The creeper of sacred arts and learning, whose network of roots had been severed by the harsh influence of the Kali age, sprouted fresh leaves again when nourished by the nectar-like sprinkling of his speech.

32.sa: ललाटरेखादम्भेन बिरुदाक्षरशालिनः । जयस्तम्भायिता यस्य प्रतिधीराः पराजिताः ॥ ३२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Many scholars who ventured to confront Sri Raghavendra in disputations were defeated (fled from the place) as they could not contend with his dexterity in debating. This resulted in a sense of astonishment and disbelief in them which was apparent in the form of wrinkles on their foreheads. Those wrinkles appeared to proclaim the fact that those scholars were defeated by Sri Raghavendra. When they returned to their places with those wrinkles still on their foreheads, they appeared like victory columns erected all over to spread the message of Sri Raghavendra's triumph over them.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: ललाटरेखादम्भेन बिरुद-अक्षर-शालिनः जयस्तम्भायिताः यस्य प्रतिधीराः पराजिताः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यस्य पराजिताः प्रतिधीराः ललाटरेखादम्भेन बिरुदाक्षरशालिनः जयस्तम्भायिताः (अभवन्)।
commentaries.gemini_summary: The rival scholars defeated by Sri Raghavendra turned into living victory pillars, bearing his inscriptions of victory in the guise of the furrowed lines on their foreheads.

33.sa: श्रोतॄणां श्रवणान्यासन् यद्वागमृतसेवया । नित्यापि तदयोग्यत्वान्न तथाहीन्द्रियान्तरम् ॥ ३३ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The ears of those who regularly listens to the ambrosial discourses of Sri Raghavendra have attained perpetuity whereas the other organs such as eyes, nose, etc., which does not enjoy such privilege have failed to achieve eternity. This confirmed the fact that the words of Sri Raghavendra serve as ambrosia for those who have the privilege of constantly listening to them.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: श्रोतॄणाम् श्रवणानि आसन् यद्-वाक्-अमृत-सेवया नित्या अपि तत्-अयोग्यत्वात् न तथा हि इन्द्रिय-अन्तरम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यद्-वाक्-अमृत-सेवया श्रोतॄणां श्रवणानि नित्यानि आसन् हि, तत्-अयोग्यत्वात् इन्द्रियान्तरं तथा न (आसीत्) ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: By partaking of the nectar of his discourses, the ears of the listeners attained immortality, whereas their other sense organs, being incapable of drinking that verbal nectar, did not.

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The antagonists of Sri Raghavendra in disputations are like oceans. Debating with those antagonists, Sri Raghavendra churned them with the Mandara parvatha of his points of view just like the suras and asuras churning the ocean with the real Mandara parvatha. If the churning by them produced ambrosia, Sri Raghavendra had his fame spread to all the comers for his dexterity in debating.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: प्रतीपविद्वत्पाथोधिमथनोत्सवचुञ्चुना वाद-मन्दर-शैलेन येन अवापि यशः अमृतम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: प्रतीपविद्वत्पाथोधिमथनोत्सवचुञ्चुना वादमन्दरशैलेन येन यशः अमृतम् अवापि ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: By acting as the Mandara mountain in debates—expert in the celebration of churning the ocean of opposing scholars—Sri Raghavendra obtained the nectar of fame.

35.sa: हिरण्यगर्भमूर्तिस्थपुरुषस्येव यद्यशः । ततो बहिः प्रस्त्रमरं राजते रौप्यसंपुटम् ॥ ३५ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: The universe is the body of Chathurmuka Brahma, wherein Lord Sri Hari pervades. These dazzling fame of Sri Raghavendra which has spread even outside the universe is glittering like a silver case with the Lord within it. Or, the dazzling fame of Sri Raghavendra which has spread even outside the sacred Saligrama wherein Lord Sri Hari pervades is glittering like a silver case in which the Saligrama is kept.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: हिरण्यगर्भ-मूर्ति-स्थ-पुरुषस्य इव यत्-यशः ततः बहिः प्रस्त्रमरम् राजते रौप्य-सम्पुटम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: ततः बहिः प्रस्त्रमरं यद्यशः हिरण्यगर्भमूर्तिस्थपुरुषस्य रौप्यसम्पुटम् इव राजते ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Raghavendra's immaculate fame, spreading extensively beyond the universe where the Supreme Lord resides within the cosmic form, shines brilliantly like a radiant silver casket enclosing the Lord.

36.sa: गुरुराद्यः स्वसिद्धान्तप्रतिष्ठापनपण्डितम् । श्रुत्वा यं व्यासनिकटे निश्चिन्त इव वर्तते ॥ ३६ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Madhwacharya, the great guru has full faith in Sri Raghavendra's competence in substantiating his philosophy of dualism. Therefore he has decided to stay with Lord Sri Vedavyasa without entertaining any anxious thoughts.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: गुरुः आद्यः स्वसिद्धान्तप्रतिष्ठापनपण्डितम् श्रुत्वा यम् व्यासनिकटे निश्चिन्तः इव वर्तते
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: आद्यः गुरुः यम् स्वसिद्धान्तप्रतिष्ठापनपण्डितम् श्रुत्वा व्यासनिकटे निश्चिन्तः इव वर्तते
commentaries.gemini_summary: The founding preceptor, Sri Madhvacharya, having learned of Raghavendra's expertise in firmly establishing his philosophical system, stays in the company of Sri Vyasa as though completely free of worry.

37.sa: गोपायति दृढं यस्मिन्नवनीदेवताकुलम् । शयानः शेषशय्यायां निद्रातीव हरिश्चिरम् ॥ ३७ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: All the brahmins were being well protected by Sri Raghavendra. Hence Lord Sri Narayana appeared as if he is sleeping leisurely on his couch of Sesha in Shewtadweepa assigning his task of protection of the world to Sri Raghavendra.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: गोपायति दृढम् यस्मिन् अवनीदेवता-कुलम् शयानः शेष-शय्यायाम् निद्राति इव हरिः चिरम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यस्मिन् अवनीदेवता-कुलम् दृढम् गोपायति (सति), शेष-शय्यायाम् शयानः हरिः चिरम् निद्राति इव।
commentaries.gemini_summary: As Sri Raghavendra securely protected the entire community of Brahmins, Lord Hari, reclining comfortably on His serpent-bed, appeared to be sleeping in deep, carefree slumber.

38.sa: पदेपदे प्रपन्नानां संपदः स्मृतिसंभवाः । परीभावप्रदे यस्मिन् शैले शेते नु शंकरः ॥ ३८ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Sri Raghavendra blesses those who surrender at his lotus feet with wealth if they just chant his name. Then those who worship him constantly are sure to be blessed with opulence more than what Shiva, the bestower of wealth would have bestowed. As a result of this, it appears as if Shiva having felt offended is sleeping in Rajatadri in resentment.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: पदे पदे प्रपन्नानाम् संपदः स्मृतिसंभवाः परीभावप्रदे यस्मिन् शैले शेते नु शंकरः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: परीभावप्रदे यस्मिन् प्रपन्नानाम् पदे पदे स्मृतिसंभवाः संपदः (भवन्ति), (ततः) शंकरः शैले शेते नु ?
commentaries.gemini_summary: For those who take refuge in Sri Raghavendra, fortunes arise at every step from mere remembrance of him; it is as if Lord Shiva, feeling completely outdone by his benevolence, has retired to sleep away on Mount Kailasa.

39.sa: व्याख्यां प्रख्याप्य विख्यातो संख्यावत्सु यदीरिताम् । सुरलोके सुरगुरुः पाताले फणिनां पतिः ॥ ३९ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Brihaspathyacharya and Sesha, the king of snakes earned fame as great scholars by imparting lessions on the points of view of Sri Raghavendra in his commentaries on Sutrabhashya in conformity with the teachings of Sri Madhwacharya to their disciples at Devaloka and Pathalaloka. This establishes the fact that it was Sri Raghavendra who wrote commentaries in conformity with the views of Sri Madhwacharya whose fame has spread to all the three lokas.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: व्याख्याम् प्रख्याप्य विख्यातौ संख्यावत्सु यत्-ईरिताम् सुरलोके सुरगुरुः पाताले फणिनाम् पतिः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: सुरलोके सुरगुरुः पाताले फणिनाम् पतिः च यदीरिताम् व्याख्याम् प्रख्याप्य संख्यावत्सु विख्यातौ (अभवताम्)।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Brihaspati in the celestial realm and Adi-Sesha in the netherworld attained renown among the learned by expounding the commentaries composed by Sri Raghavendra.

40.sa: चित्ते चेन्मृदुता शिरीषसदृशे हैयंगवीनं शिला- गाम्भीर्यं यदि यस्य सोन्धुरुदधीः शास्त्रेषु चेत्पाण्डिती । आचार्यो विबुधेशितुः कलयते विद्यार्थितामादरा- दौदार्यं यदि कल्पपादपमुखाः संभावयन्तेऽर्थिताम् ॥ ४० ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: Ghee is known for its softness. But when viewed in comparision with the softness of Sri Raghavendra's mind which is like that of Shireesha flower, fresh ghee looks like stone. The ocean reputed for its majesty looks like a well before the majesty of Sri Raghavendra.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: चित्ते चेत् मृदुता शिरीष-सदृशे हैयङ्गवीनम् शिला गाम्भीर्यम् यदि यस्य सः अन्धुः उदधिः शास्त्रेषु चेत् पाण्डिती आचार्यः विबुध-ईशितुः कलयते विद्यार्थिताम् आदरात् औदार्यम् यदि कल्प-पादप-मुखाः सम्भावयन्ते अर्थिताम्
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: यस्य शिरीष-सदृशे चित्ते मृदुता चेत् हैयङ्गवीनं शिला (भवति), यदि गाम्भीर्यं (तर्हि) सः उदधिः अन्धुः (भवति), शास्त्रेषु पाण्डिती चेत् विबुध-ईशितुः आचार्यः आदरात् विद्यार्थितां कलयते, यदि औदार्यं (तर्हि) कल्प-पादप-मुखाः अर्थितां सम्भावयन्ते ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Compared to the tender softness of his mind, fresh butter seems hard as stone; beside his profound depth, the ocean is a mere well; before his erudition, Brihaspati assumes the humility of a student; and in contrast to his immense generosity, the wish-fulfilling Kalpavriksha and other celestial trees seem like supplicants.

41.sa: तस्मान्महामहिम्नेऽस्मै मनः स्पृहयते मम । तद्गौरवेण मत्काव्यमङ्गीकुर्वन्तु सज्जनाः ॥ ४१ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: If Brihaspathyacharya, the guru of Devendra thinks about the erudite scholarship of Sri Raghavendra, he would yearn to become the disciple of the saint out of admiration for his scholarship. The thought about Sri Raghavendra's magnanimity makes one to feel that the five trees of heaven - Mandara, Parijatha, Santana, Kalpavruksha, Chandana as well as Kamadhenu and Chintamani which fulfil the wishes of the suppliants would like to pray Sri Raghavendra to fulfil the wishes of those suppliants. This is how the poet has extolled the kindness, majesty, erudition and magnanimity of Sri Raghavendra.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: तस्मात् महामहिम्ने अस्मै मनः स्पृहयते मम । तत्-गौरवेण मत्-काव्यम् अङ्गीकुर्वन्तु सज्जनाः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: तस्मात् अस्मै महामहिम्ने मम मनः स्पृहयते । सज्जनाः तद्गौरवेण मत्काव्यम् अङ्गीकुर्वन्तु ।
commentaries.gemini_summary: Therefore, my mind yearns for this person of supreme greatness; may virtuous people accept my poem out of reverence for him.

42.sa: श्रीमत्कश्यपवंशवार्धिशशिनः षड्दर्शनीवल्लभ- श्रीलक्ष्मीनरसिंहवित्तविदुषः श्रीवेङ्कटाम्बामणौ । जातेनार्यदयासुधामयगिरा नारायणेनोदिते काव्ये चारुणि राघवेन्द्रविजये सर्गो जयत्यादिमः ॥ ४२ ॥

commentaries.pavamanacharya_english: It is my earnest desire to praise my guru of such virtues. I wish that all the men and women of moral excellence out of their reverence for Sri Raghavendra and also taking into account the significance of this poetry accept my composition wherein I have given a detailed account of the divine prowess of the great guru.
commentaries.gemini_padaccheda: श्रीमत्-कश्यप-वंश-वार्धि-शशिनः षड्दर्शनी-वल्लभ-श्री-लक्ष्मीनरसिंह-वित्त-विदुषः श्री-वेङ्कटाम्बा-मणौ जातेन आर्य-दया-सुधा-मय-गिरा नारायणेन उदिते काव्ये चारुणि राघवेन्द्र-विजये सर्गः जयति आदिमः
commentaries.gemini_anvaya: श्रीमत्-कश्यप-वंश-वार्धि-शशिनः षड्दर्शनी-वल्लभ-श्री-लक्ष्मीनरसिंह-वित्त-विदुषः श्री-वेङ्कटाम्बा-मणौ जातेन आर्य-दया-सुधा-मय-गिरा नारायणेन उदिते चारुणि राघवेन्द्र-विजये काव्ये आदिमः सर्गः जयति।
commentaries.gemini_summary: This concluding verse marks the triumphant completion of the first canto of the charming epic poem 'Raghavendra Vijaya', composed by Narayana, the son of the scholar Lakshmi Narasimha (the moon to the Kashyapa lineage) and Venkatamba, blessed with nectar-like speech through the grace of the noble.
